name: Ferrochem NovaClear Fab Cleanroom Suit Type-F
description:
A Tier 3–4 cleanroom enclosure suit for chip fabrication floors and geneware synthesis labs. Constructed from triple-layered antistatic polyfilm over a breathable HEPA-bonded inner lining, the NovaClear is sealed at every joint with ultrasonic-welded gaskets. Color is uniform pale blue-white with Ferrochem's teal stripe along the outer arms and legs.

The hood integrates a positive-pressure filtered air supply and a wide visor with anti-fog coating. Glove ports accept standard or aug-interface gauntlets. The suit is rated Class 10 particulate.
functionality: Class 10 particulate rating blocks contaminants down to 0.1 microns. Positive-pressure air supply prevents inward contamination. Antistatic outer shell protects sensitive fab components. Glove ports are aug-compatible for chrome-hand technicians. Integrated humidity sensor alerts to seal degradation.
what_it_says: Someone who works in a controlled environment worth more per square meter than most people earn in a year.
story_hooks: A technician has been smuggling out single-use polyfilm panels to sell to the Gray Zone medics who use them as sterile wound covers.
The suit's air supply logged an anomalous atmospheric compound during a recent shift — one that shouldn't exist in a sealed fab.
Someone has been leaving unmarked data chips inside the glove ports before shift changes.

physical_description.visual_profile: A full-body enclosure suit with a distinctive clean-room silhouette—boxy, geometric, utterly functional. The pale blue-white base reads clinical and sterile, grounded by teal racing stripes that run down the outer arms and legs, creating a subtle speed-line effect even at rest. The integrated hood dominates the upper body, featuring a large rectangular visor that gives the wearer an almost insectoid appearance. On-body, the suit reads institutional, precise, and undeniably corpo.
physical_description.fit: Roomy through the torso and limbs to accommodate layered undergarments and movement, but tapered at the wrists and ankles with compression gaskets. The overall silhouette is boxy and geometric—no body contouring, prioritizing seal integrity over aesthetics.
physical_description.primary_material: Triple-layered antistatic polyfilm exterior over HEPA-bonded breathable lining. The outer membrane is glossy and slightly reflective; the inner surfaces are matte and tactile.
physical_description.texture: The polyfilm exterior is smooth and frictionless with a faint waffle-weave pattern (antistatic grid). Gasket seams are visibly ultrasonic-welded with a slight ribbed texture at each joint. Where the fabric creases, faint stress lines emerge but never tear.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pale blue-white (almost clinical off-white with a cool blue undertone) as the dominant color. A teal accent stripe (Ferrochem corporate cyan) runs the full length of both outer arms and legs. The visor has a faint amber tint from the anti-fog coating.
closures: Ultrasonic-welded gaskets at neck, wrists, and ankles
Magnetic snap closures down the front centerline
Friction-fit hood seal around the face opening
distinctive_features: Integrated positive-pressure hood with wide rectangular visor
Anti-fog coated polycarbonate visor with subtle yellow tint
Glove ports with standard locking rings (accept gauntlets or aug-interface adapters)
Ferrochem embossed logo on left chest (teal on white)
Class 10 particulate rating stamp on inner collar
HEPA filter cartridge port on left shoulder (quick-swap design)
Pressure-relief micro-vent on lower back (barely visible)
Teal piping along all major seams for visual continuity and branding
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 functional corpo issue. The suit is expensive enough to signal factory-floor employment or specialized lab work, but ubiquitous enough within Ferrochem facilities that it doesn't confer individual status. It's the uniform of precision work.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this marks you as either a fab technician, geneware synthesis operator, or contamination-control specialist. It signals compliance with corporate safety protocols, precision training, and authorized access to high-value manufacturing floors. To street-level observers, it reads as 'dangerous work, corpo-vetted, off-limits to outsiders.'
physical_description.condition_typical: When new: pristine, with visible creases from packaging and a faint plastic smell. After a few shifts: micro-scratches on the visor from casual contact, slight discoloration at the wrist gaskets from sweat buildup (despite the lining), possible teal stripe fading along high-contact areas. Long-term: welded seams may show stress cracks if the suit is reused; the visor acquires a permanent haze despite anti-fog treatment; patches (authorized repair tape in matching blue-white) appear at wear points.
